name: adapters
description: The adapter contract, plus a reference adapter. The receipts wire-format constants live in a Go package compiled into spex; the adapters themselves are scripts outside the binary. Each adapter has two halves: an export half that derives the task-state artifact plan reads from the tracker, and an apply half that consumes changeset.json, executes the tool-specific subcommands against the tracker, and writes receipts.json. The adapter is the one place a tracker's own format is read or written. The current reference adapter targets br; authors of adapters for other trackers (bd, GitHub Issues, Jira) consult the same task-state/changeset/receipts contracts without changes to spex. Requirements in this module double as the contract any adapter must satisfy.

requirements.name: Read changeset v1
requirements.description: The adapter parses changeset.json v4 and refuses earlier or later versions with a clear error — refusal is the whole point of the version field, because a consumer that silently dropped ops it does not know (v2 meeting a retarget) or resolved refs it does not know (v3 meeting a task ref) would report a complete run over an incomplete one. It reads ops in the order given and processes them sequentially — order matters because later ops may forward-reference earlier op results. The op vocabulary is create, close and retarget; anything else is an error receipt, never a silent skip. The top-level absorbed array is not the adapter's: it is ignored entirely and consumed by ingest. The title's version is identity-bearing legacy; four is the contract.

requirements.name: Op ID substitution table
requirements.description: As the adapter processes create ops, it maintains an op_id → task_id substitution table. When a later op's deps or parent contains {"ref":"op","op_id":"<id>"}, the adapter resolves the ref from this table. Missing table entries (e.g., the referenced op was skipped or errored) cause the dependent op to be downgraded to error with a clear reason.

requirements.name: Resolve three ref shapes
requirements.description: For each ref field in parent, deps and a retarget's target: {"ref":"task","task_id":"<id>"} resolves as-is; {"ref":"op","op_id":"<id>"} resolves via the substitution table. The changeset carries no third shape — plan resolves spec-node references in-process before the adapter runs, so the adapter reads no spex-owned file — and a ref carries no edge-type field: every dep is the tracker's default blocking edge. The title's count is identity-bearing legacy; two shapes is the contract.

requirements.name: Idempotent create via label
requirements.description: The create-idempotency probe is an optional adapter capability: the changeset's idempotency.label is insurance, not a conformance bar, and an adapter for a tracker without label support omits the probe entirely — accepting that a run crashed between a create and its receipt can duplicate that create on a blind re-run. The reference adapter implements it: before creating a task for a create op, it queries the tracker for an existing task carrying the op's idempotency.label — an exact string match, in any tracker status; the adapter treats the label as opaque and does not parse it. The open-only filter of the node-keyed label era is gone with the collisions it existed to dodge: a label is spex:<eid>, unique per change, so any task carrying it — live or finished — can only be the product of this same op's earlier run. On match: skip the create, record was_existing=true with the existing task_id in the receipt. On no match: create the task, record was_existing=false with the new task_id. Re-runs of a partial changeset are safe: already-created tasks are not duplicated.

requirements.name: Idempotent close via label
requirements.description: Close idempotency keys on the tracker's own status, not on any label — the close markers of the label era are retired, and close ops carry no labels (the title's via-label wording is identity-bearing legacy). Before closing a task for a close op, the adapter reads the target's current state. Already closed in the tracker: skip the transition, record status=ok — whichever run closed it, a close op against a closed task converges. Open: close it, carrying the op's reason when one is present. This guards the crash-between-close-and-receipt scenario the same way the label did: a second run sees the closed task and records the skip correctly. A close op is only ever issued for a task plan read as live, so the converging branch is the re-run case alone, never routine.

requirements.name: Write receipts v1
requirements.description: For each op processed (or failed), the adapter records a per-op entry with op_id, status (ok|skipped|error), task_id (if applicable), was_existing (for create ops), and an optional error or reason string; the document carries version 2, the version that renamed the per-op tracker id field to task_id, and ingest refuses any other (the title's version is identity-bearing legacy; two is the contract). The entries are accumulated and receipts.json is written once, after the last op. The top-level status field is complete if every op produced ok or intentional-skipped, partial if any op resulted in error. An adapter that exits before the last op writes no receipts file at all; spex ingest then fails with ingest: read receipts: ... no such file or directory and exit 1, so an aborted adapter run must be re-run, not ingested.

requirements.name: Integration test against real br
requirements.description: A shell-based integration test (scripts/apply-br_test.sh) exercises the full adapter against a real br sandbox. It validates: the export half's task-state artifact against the live listing, changeset parsing, both ref shapes resolving correctly, idempotency on re-run, a retarget op relabelling an open task and adding only the dependencies it does not yet carry, receipt output matches the v2 receipts schema, and partial-receipt handling when a synthetic failure is injected mid-run. The test is gated on br being present on PATH and is excluded from the Go test suite.

requirements.name: Reference implementation scope
requirements.description: scripts/apply-br.sh is explicitly marked as a reference implementation — vet before production use. It demonstrates the required adapter contract but does not aspire to handle every tracker misconfiguration. Users wanting production-grade adapters for their environment should fork and adapt. The contract (this module's functional requirements) is the authoritative specification that any adapter must meet.

requirements.name: Apply retarget ops
requirements.description: A retarget op names an existing task in its target ref and the adapter translates it to the tracker's mutation surface: add the op's spex:<eid> event label to the task where the tracker supports labels — the label half is optional linkage an adapter without labels skips — and add any deps the task does not already carry. The two halves need not be one call — for br the label goes through br update and each dep through br dep add, because br update carries no dep flag — and a dep edge is named in the tracker's own dep-type vocabulary, not the changeset's spelling. Deps are add-only; nothing is removed, because stale deps are closed by their own lifecycle. Both calls are naturally idempotent, so retarget needs no pre-create probe: re-applying the same retarget adds nothing new. The receipt records op_id, status and the target task_id; was_existing does not apply to retargets.

components.name: BrReferenceAdapter
components.description: Bash + jq implementation of the adapter contract targeting br, in two halves. The export half, scripts/export-br.sh, derives the task-state artifact from br list: filtered to open and in_progress, projected to task_id and status, written as the version-1 task-state document. The apply half, scripts/apply-br.sh, reads changeset.json v4, resolves refs via the substitution table, runs br create/list/show/update/dep add/close for each op — a retarget op becomes a br update adding the new event label plus one br dep add per missing dep — and writes receipts.json v2. br's own name for what it manages never enters the contract: the scripts speak br's surface through its command strings and call what they manage tasks. Integration-tested against a real br sandbox via scripts/apply-br_test.sh.

data_flows.name: Adapter flow
data_flows.description: Export, before plan: tracker listing → filter to in-flight statuses → project to task_id and status → tasks.json, the version-1 task-state document plan reads. Apply, after plan: changeset.json → parse → iterate ops in order → for each op: resolve refs, query tracker for idempotency, run subcommand, record receipt → receipts.json v2 assembled in memory and written atomically once, after the last op, so a reader sees either the whole document or the path's previous contents; a run that dies mid-loop writes nothing, and spex ingest then fails with ingest: read receipts: ... no such file or directory and exit 1, so an aborted run must be re-run rather than ingested.
